title: ECP-YOLO11n: a lightweight insulator defect detection algorithm (Scientific Reports, 2026)
page_numbers: Physical PDF page numbers (same as the page_label PyPDFLoader returns for this file).
how_to_score: q01-q25: hand-grade against ground_truth. u01-u05: pass only if the answer says I don't know.

questions.question: By what percentage does ECP-YOLO11n cut the parameter count compared with the YOLO11n baseline?
By how much does ECP-YOLO11n cut the computational cost, and how much of the original mAP50 does it keep on CPLID-2000 and IDID?
questions.ground_truth: Computational cost is cut by 23.8%; it keeps 99.5% (CPLID-2000) and 95.1% (IDID) of the original mAP50.

questions.question: On what date did Ultralytics release YOLO11?
questions.ground_truth: September 10, 2024.

questions.question: What are the three contributions listed for ECP-YOLO11n?
questions.ground_truth: (1) EMA attention in the Neck fusion layer; (2) the C3Ghost module replaces C3k2 in the Neck; (3) a Progressive Channel Compression strategy for the backbone.

questions.question: What channel reduction factors (lambda) are used for the P4 and P5 layers of the backbone?
questions.ground_truth: 0.75 for P4 (layers 5 and 6) and 0.5 for P5 (layers 7 and 8).

questions.question: How did the authors find out that the deep channels of the baseline are redundant?
questions.ground_truth: They ran sparse training with L1 regularization on the scaling factor gamma of Batch Normalization and saw that more than 45% of channels in P4, P5 and SPPF had similar gamma values.

questions.question: What is the overall channel scaling factor of YOLO11n, and what does it mean for the actual number of training channels?
questions.ground_truth: 0.25, so the actual number of training channels is a quarter of the numbers in Table 1.

questions.question: What inference speedup does C3Ghost give over C3k2 for a single module and for the whole Neck?
questions.ground_truth: 1.79 times for a single module and 1.63 times for the whole Neck.

questions.question: In Table 2, what are the GFLOPs and real XPU time of C3k2 and C3Ghost for a 64x80x80 input?
questions.ground_truth: C3k2: 0.051 GFLOPs and 0.25 ms; C3Ghost: 0.027 GFLOPs and 0.14 ms.

questions.question: At which layers is EMA inserted and what feature map sizes does it take (Table 3)?
questions.ground_truth: Layer 13 (P4/16, medium targets) with 96x40x40, and layer 17 (P3/8, small targets) with 64x80x80.

questions.question: Why do the authors not put EMA on the P5 branch?
questions.ground_truth: The P5 resolution (20x20) is too low and small targets have nearly disappeared there; adding EMA there also raises the computational burden a lot.

questions.question: What batch size, number of epochs, optimizer and input image size are used for training?
questions.ground_truth: Batch size 16, 100 epochs, SGD optimizer, image size 640.
evidence: batch size is uniformly set to 16

questions.question: What computer hardware and software were the experiments run on?
questions.ground_truth: Windows 11, Intel Core Ultra 7 155 H CPU, 32 GB RAM, Intel Arc Graphics GPU with 18 GB video memory, PyTorch-triton-xpu 3.3.0 and Python 3.13.

questions.question: How many images does the original CPLID dataset have, how is it split, and how big is CPLID-2000 after expansion?
questions.ground_truth: 848 images split 678 train, 85 validation, 85 test; expanded to 1600 train, 200 validation and 200 test images, 2000 in total.

questions.question: How many images does the IDID dataset have, which three categories does it include, and what is its split?
questions.ground_truth: 1600 images; categories pollution-flashover, broken and insulator; split 8:1:1.

questions.question: Which datasets are used, and what FPS does the final model reach on each?
questions.ground_truth: CPLID-2000 and IDID; the final model reaches 27.64 FPS on CPLID-2000 and 40.61 FPS on IDID.

questions.question: On CPLID-2000, what are the mAP50, parameters, GFLOPs and FPS of the final scheme 6 in Table 7?
questions.ground_truth: mAP50 97.3%, 1.04 M parameters, 4.8 GFLOPs and 27.64 FPS.

questions.question: On IDID, how much does mAP50 fall with channel compression alone, and what does adding EMA to scheme 5 give?
questions.ground_truth: With channel compression alone mAP50 falls from 81.6% to 73.6% (a drop of 8.0%); adding EMA to scheme 5 raises mAP50 from 75.1% to 77.6%.

questions.question: How much do parameters drop when only channel compression is used, and by what percentage?
questions.ground_truth: From 2.58 M to 1.10 M, a reduction of 57.4%.

questions.question: How is the final model checkpoint chosen?
questions.ground_truth: As the checkpoint with the highest fitness (0.1 x mAP50-95 plus 0.9 x mAP50) on the validation set.

questions.question: How does the speed of the final model compare with Faster R-CNN on CPLID-2000 and IDID?
questions.ground_truth: On CPLID-2000 it runs 27.64 FPS versus 5.64 FPS (nearly 5 times faster); on IDID 40.61 FPS versus 7.12 FPS (more than 5 times faster).

questions.question: What three typical failure modes of the model are named in the Discussion?
questions.ground_truth: Illumination and viewpoint change, image blur, and partial occlusion.

questions.question: By how much are the P4 and P5 channel counts cut in the backbone and in the detection head?
questions.ground_truth: Backbone: P4 from 512 to 384 and P5 from 1024 to 512. Detection head: P4 from 512 to 384 channels and P5 from 1024 to 512 channels (P3 stays at 256).

questions.question: What fraction of the YOLO11n parameter count does the final model have, and what parameter reduction does the abstract report?
questions.ground_truth: The final model has 1.04 M parameters, 40.3% of YOLO11n; the abstract reports a 59.7% reduction in parameters.

questions.question: Which attention module is added to the Neck, and what limit of the channel reduction do the authors admit in the Discussion?
questions.ground_truth: The Efficient Multi-Scale Attention (EMA) module; the channel reduction limits the ability of the network to represent high-order global semantics, so the model leans on shallow texture features against cluttered backgrounds.
evidence: limits the ability of the network

questions.question: What mAP50 does ECP-YOLO11n reach on the COCO dataset?
questions.ground_truth: I don't know.
questions.note: The paper only mentions COCO as the dataset YOLO11n was designed for; it reports no COCO result.

questions.question: Which drone model was used for the real flight tests of ECP-YOLO11n?
questions.ground_truth: I don't know.
questions.note: No drone model is named; the model was only tested on a laptop-class Intel platform.

questions.ground_truth: I don't know.
